speaker: will_kemp
text: Give it here, then. I can see it is fair. Fair is how a will looks.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: The roll is recopied. Nine of your lines are in the book. Two are out.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You've set down what I made up. Now I can't make it up.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You can make up something new, Will. I'll set that down at Easter.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And then?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we'll have a long play.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Only nine. On Shrove Tuesday the yard had the rest of them for nothing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The rest are not in the book. I cut two. I am not telling the cut over again until I have to.

speaker: will_kemp
text: If the cut stands, then after Easter I will give you three minutes of shin-scratching with a turnip, and the yard will thank me.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The Rose is playing that king's part today. Hear what this house does with a voice.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: This house likes a king.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It likes a king when the yard is empty and the voice is thine. Do not teach it a habit we are not paying for.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: I am tired of French rhymes. I want an English king whose crown burns his forehead. Something to wash Tamburlaine out of London's mouth, and not thy hunchback again.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not this week. The page that is open at home is not a king.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And my way off? I will not be waved at like a tray.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: The argument has now run longer than the business. The business was two lines, and a way to leave.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: A visible cue. Not a verdict on who has won.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thy cap, Will. On the ninth line the cap comes off, and thou art gone. A yard can see a cap in the dark of a gallery.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The cap is mine. The line is now yours. I like them better when they disagree.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Then the cap is the cue, and nobody has won. I can go and be cold in another part of the house.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Write it where Abel can see it without asking thee twice.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Cap off, by the ninth. I have room in the margin. I will not set down the turnip.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The turnip is a promise, not a property. Promises do not go in the basket.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Easter. Not before. And no shin of mine, if the cap is kept.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The galleries gave the king back. Remember that, when thou art tired of clowns and of me.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will remember an empty house. Empty is an honest audience. It does not pay.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Honest and unpaid. We are in Lent. Are we finished with the two lines?

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Finished. The roll can be tied.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Tie it. And leave me the making-up of the next nine. You have had your nine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Those nine are yours. I only stopped them moving.
